narrative: Larkspur Digital's personal-shopper agent, submitted by Northgate Payments for authorisation. Thirty-six independent shopping tasks across nine weeks — AP2's human-present flow, so each run is a complete chain: the shopper's request becomes an Intent Mandate, they sign the exact cart, and the Payment Mandate carries it to the network. This is the cleanest of the three submissions and it should read that way: thirty-one runs are sound, one shopper walked away at the confirmation, one merchant returned a 502 before any mandate existed, and one purchase was stopped by Larkspur's own budget control doing exactly what it is declared to do. That last one is the contrast that matters — the same control fired on 11 August and was switched off by an analyst, which makes that a conduct question rather than a technical one. The remaining four defects are ordinary supervisory material: a confirmation screen that did not show what was signed, a tool call to a server nobody authorised, a merchant page carrying instructions aimed at the agent, and a purchase that was within budget and not the thing the shopper asked for.
